newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Slump in Belgrade bourse turnover drags index down.
newsitem.headline: Slump in Belgrade bourse turnover drags index down.

text.p: A 53 percent plunge in turnover dragged the Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) short-term debentures index down 39 index points in the week to July 25, the BSE said on Monday.
Traders attributed the slide to a declining trade in T-bills and a summer lull embracing the market.
Total turnover slumped to 47.89 million dinars ($7.89 million) from 102.75 million dinars a week ago, but the number of transactions was unchanged at 103. All trade took place on the primary market.
The recently established BSE index of short-term debentures slumped 16.39 percent to 199.23 index points from 238.29 points a week ago, the bourse said in its report.

Traders said the liquidity of the banking sector was heavily improved with commercial banks witnessing a sharp increase in sight deposits to more than 2.5 billion dinars from an average 1.6 billion a month ago.
The improved liquidity and a lack of demand pushed interest rates on commercial lending down to 5.5 to 6.5 percent per month, from an average 8.00 to 9.00 percent a month ago.
"It is evident that a 25 percent increase in deposits resulted from an additional cash injection, but it is almost impossible to see where the money came from," one dealer told Reuters.
Analysts were confident that most of the fresh funds came after the state converted into dinars part of its hard currency receipts from the sale of 49 percent stake in Telekom Srbija early in June.
The stake was sold to Italian and Greek partners for almost $1 billion.
Traders also said the cash had remained in the system rather than moving to traditional hard currency safe havens.
For the week ending July 25, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 84 times for a volume of 16.98 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for five deals worth 1.24 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between a monthly 5.80 and 9.00 percent, with maturities standing between six and 60 days.
* Central bank short-term bonds traded once for a total of one million dinars.
* State T-bills accounted for six deals worth 26.3 million dinars.
* OTC trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 64.266 billion dinars from 60.27 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, declined to 28.3 million dinars from 38.5 million.

NOTE -- The BSE short-term debentures index is calculated on volume, interest rate and maturity of the most frequently bourse-traded short-term commercial paper and treasury bills. Index base is 1996. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
($1 = 6.0657 Yugoslav dinars)
